text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Social Democrat Chancellor Franz Vranitzky says he wants to raise inheritance tax rates, defying repeated calls by his junior coalition partner, the conservative People's Party, to abolish the tax.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima wants to raise taxes on trucks when road usage fees will be lowered in January in line with European Union (EU) regulations.
- Austrian metal workers who come under the umbrella of the industry's collective agreement will get a rise of 2.6 percent from January, following agreement by unions and employers over the weekend.
- Austria's insurance industry remains largely sheltered from international competition.
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky said there was no need for a referendum on Austria joining Europe's planned single currency.
- A new 50-schilling fee on public health services, to be introduced in January, will be abolished by 1998.
- The EU has criticised Austria once again for the slow pace of liberalisation of the country's telecoms market.
- The fate of an Austrian citizen who was aboard an Ethiopian airliner that was hijacked and then crashed off the African coast remains unknown.
- Computer problems will prevent Austria from complying with the EU's Schengen treaty by January 1, Interior Minister Caspar Einem said.
- A second U.S. lung specialist will perform medical tests on President Thomas Klestil this week to determine the cause of his medical problems.
- Environment Minister Martin Bartenstein says the EU should adopt Austria's stringent environmental standards.
- Analysts see strong profit growth at motorbike maker KTM, which announced its initial public offering last week.
- Chancellor Franz Vranitzky intends to seek another term as leader of the Social Democrats next year.
